gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The prediction identifies a false lemma about pairwise distinct singular directions and proposes adding an application-specific hypothesis. Gold I003 instead concerns the separately missing converse direction of the equality characterization: starting from an admissible three-cluster configuration and proving the optimal smallest singular value. The prediction's statement that the equality characterization is unproven is only a consequence and does not diagnose that omitted converse.

Both entries identify the same false lemma: pairwise non-collinearity of the three squared vectors does not imply pairwise non-collinearity of their pairwise sums, so the three associated row-pair matrices need not have pairwise distinct right-singular directions. The prediction supplies a concrete counterexample and recognizes the resulting unsupported use in Proposition pr.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The lemma's inference from pairwise non-collinear square vectors to pairwise distinct pair-sum, and hence right-singular, directions is false; therefore the asserted all-three distinctness and its use in Case A are unsupported.
